data.name: Ismael
data.gender_notes: Ismael is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'שמעאל' (Shamu'el), which means 'God hears'. In the Bible, Ismael is the elder son of Abraham and Hagar, born to Abraham after Sarah was unable to bear children. God hears Sarah's prayer for a child, and Ismael becomes the ancestor of the Arab peoples. The name Ismael carries the meaning “God hears” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ismael usually hope their child will grow to embody god hears and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ismael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God hears.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ismael total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Ismael
in_english.long_meaning: Ismael is a name of Hebrew origin, composed of two parts: Isma - God will hear, and El - God, which signifies the father's prayer to God for his son, and holds significant spiritual meaning in Christian tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ismael" holds significant cultural importance in the Arab world. Ismael is considered the ancestor of the Arabs, and his lineage is traced back to the founding prophet of Islam, Muhammad, through his maternal grandfather Ishmael. This reflects the strong connection between Abrahamic religious traditions and Arab cultural identity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Ismael is alive in paradise and holds the role of a prophet, interceding on behalf of his people. The well of Zamzam, located in Mecca, is believed to have been provided by Ismael and his mother Hagar, and is still vital to the Islamic faith as the source of the annual hajj pilgrimage. Thus, the name Ismael carries spiritual significance as a reminder of God's promise to Abraham and as a symbol of prophethood and divine providence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ismael, in the Islamic and Judeo-Christian traditions, represents the wilderness, the outsider, the independent spirit. Named by Abraham after God's promise of a son through his bondswoman Hagar, Ismael's story underscores the divine providence that shapes even the most unexpected paths of our lives.

biblical_reference.note: Ismael is the son of Abraham and Hagar, and his name is given by the angel of the Lord

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ismael is of Islamic and Middle Eastern origin and is derived from the Bible as the name of the firstborn son of Abraham and Hagar. It is commonly used in the Middle East and North Africa. In modern times, the name Ismael has become popular beyond its traditional cultural contexts due to its association with Islamic and Middle Eastern cultures and the increasing multiculturalism and globalization. Ismael is now seen on various platforms such as social media, baby naming websites, and multicultural communities. On social media, the name Ismael is used by individuals to express their cultural identity and heritage. On baby naming websites, Ismael is often listed as a popular name for boys due to its unique and exotic sound. In multicultural communities, Ismael is embraced as a name that represents the diversity and richness of different cultures and backgrounds.
